fields.description:
## Problem

`infra/terraform/bedrock-spend-cap/handler.py` prices CloudWatch token counts
using a rate table derived daily from Cost Explorer and matched to models by
string heuristics. In the twelve days since the cap was deployed (2026-09-12)
that layer produced four defects, all one class — matching model identifiers to
billing labels by substring and suffix:

1. `_rate_for`/`_match`: candidate `input-token-count` also matches
   `...-cache-write-input-token-count`, longest match wins, so input resolves to
   cache-write for any ModelId lacking a version suffix.
2. `_normalise`: `Nova2.0Lite` and `us.amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0` normalise so
   neither contains the other, dropping the model to `UNKNOWN_RATE_PER_1K`.
3. `BEDROCK_SERVICE_VALUES` (from 3083-ada3-3a0f-4051) omits five live services,
   leaving the CE signal at about a third of real spend.
4. `MARKETPLACE_TOKEN_SUFFIXES` handles only CamelCase, skipping the snake_case
   and `_Global` usage types AWS also bills.

Two reached production unalarmed, one for seven days.

## Approach

Delete the pricing-derivation layer. Price every token at a ceiling rate for its
direction, set above the highest per-direction rate observed on this account, so
the estimate is an upper bound and the cap cannot fire late. Per UTC day:

    spend = max( sum over regions and the four token metrics of
                   undimensioned CloudWatch Sum * CEILING[metric],
                 ce_spend )

`AWS/Bedrock` does publish a zero-dimension series per token metric; over
2026-09-14 to 09-24 it equalled the sum of the per-ModelId series exactly
(930,831,660 tokens both ways). The estimate reads exactly those four aggregates
per region and never adds per-ModelId series to the total — today's handler reads
only per-ModelId series precisely because mixing the two double-counts.

Cost Explorer stays in enforcement: it is the only signal covering Bedrock spend
that publishes no token metric (Cohere Rerank is live; provisioned throughput and
batch are structural), and it is orthogonal to all four defects.

**Release discriminator.** An all-empty CloudWatch read is ambiguous: it is both a
metrics gap and the normal idle/new-UTC-day state the automatic release depends
on. CE cannot disambiguate it, because CE lags 8-24h and reads zero for hours into
a busy day. Instead the handler persists the day's highest observed token total: an
empty read may release only when no earlier tick that UTC day observed tokens; once
a nonzero total has been seen, a later empty read is a gap and the deny is held. A
partial-region failure holds the deny, since the surviving region is a floor.

**Accepted limitation.** Ceiling pricing over-estimates for models much cheaper
than the priciest — the cheapest here are two orders of magnitude below, and two
bill nothing for cache-write, so the factor is unbounded. A large embedding or
small-model batch job can trip the cap at a small fraction of intended spend.
Accepted for simplicity; the remedy if it bites is an exact-match
`{ModelId: rate}` override defaulting to the ceiling, equality only. Documenting
this, the recorded fixtures and the drift guard are the dependent hardening story.

## Figures

Machine-local policy bars spend totals and bill figures from the tracker, because
the tickets branch auto-pushes to the public GitHub mirror. All three inputs are
derivable, so no executor depends on a private note:

- intended daily cap: the value already configured as `var.bedrock_daily_cap_usd`
  in `infra/terraform/bedrock_spend_cap.tf`, which this ticket does not change.
- `CEILING[d]`: 1.25x the highest per-token rate for direction `d` across all
  Bedrock services in the trailing 60 days of Cost Explorer.
- threshold: the intended daily cap scaled by the median, over the same window and
  over days above a small spend floor, of (undimensioned tokens x CEILING) divided
  by the CE Bedrock total for that UTC day.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The seven pricing functions (`_refresh_rates`, `_rate_for`, `_seed_for`,
  `_normalise`, `_strip_billing_region`, `_marketplace_rate_key`,
  `_rate_key_for_ce_group`) and six constants (`SEED_RATES`, `RATE_OVERRIDES`,
  `BEDROCK_SERVICE_VALUES`, `MARKETPLACE_TOKEN_SUFFIXES`, `UNKNOWN_RATE_PER_1K`,
  `MARKETPLACE_TOKENS_PER_RATE_UNIT`) are absent from the module.
- [ ] The `TOKEN_METRICS` direction multipliers are removed.
- [ ] `_metered_spend` issues exactly four undimensioned `GetMetricData` queries
  per region.
- [ ] `_metered_spend` calls no `list_metrics`.
- [ ] A `CEILING` mapping gives one rate per token metric, each at least the
  highest rate for that direction over the trailing 60 days of Cost Explorer,
  with the derivation recorded as a comment beside it.
- [ ] Enforcement compares `max(ceiling_estimate, ce_spend)`. Checked: a test
  driving each arm larger in turn.
- [ ] `_ce_spend_today` classifies Bedrock spend by predicate (service equals
  `Amazon Bedrock` or ends with the Bedrock Edition suffix), not an allowlist.
  Checked: a test over a stubbed response carrying all ten live services,
  including the five the allowlist omitted.
- [ ] An all-empty read with no earlier nonzero reading that UTC day may release.
  Checked: a test on a fresh day with an empty read.
- [ ] An all-empty read after an earlier nonzero reading that day holds the deny.
  Checked: a test seeding the persisted high-water mark.
- [ ] A partial-region failure holds the deny. Checked: a test raising in one
  region while the other returns data below threshold.
- [ ] Any exception from a metered or CE read fails closed. Checked: a test
  raising from each client in turn.
- [ ] The first tick after deploy tolerates state written by the old handler,
  ignoring its rate keys. Checked: a test loading a pre-change state document.
- [ ] `infra/terraform/bedrock_spend_cap.tf` carries the threshold and warning
  values derived above.
- [ ] The `SEED_RATES`, `RATE_OVERRIDES`, `UNKNOWN_RATE_PER_1K` and
  `RATE_WINDOW_DAYS` environment entries are deleted, along with whichever
  `variable` or `locals` blocks are left with no remaining reference. Checked:
  `terraform plan` shows exactly those deletions plus the threshold and warning
  changes.
- [ ] No unused Terraform declarations remain. Checked: `terraform validate`.
- [ ] `state["rates"]`, `state["rates_day"]`, `metered_estimated`, `MeteredRate`
  and its `RateSource` alias, and the `" (estimated)"` rendering are removed.

## Testing

Every criterion above is proved by
`env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/infra/test_bedrock_spend_cap_handler.py -q`,
except the two Terraform ones, proved by `terraform plan` and `terraform validate`
through `python3 scripts/terraform_prod.py plan --out <scratch>/plan.tfplan`.
`make lint` and `make typecheck` are the commit gate; `make verify` runs before
push per AGENTS.md.

## Rollback

Immediate mitigation: set `DRY_RUN=true`, halting attach and detach while leaving
the function observable. Full back-out: revert the Gerrit change and re-run the
mediated plan and apply; Terraform packages the handler by content hash, so the
revert restores prior code and env exactly.
fields.title: Price the Bedrock spend cap at a per-direction ceiling and delete the pricing-derivation layer
